# SoloBrief

> Independent reviews, comparisons and free calculators covering AI tools for
> freelancers, solopreneurs and one-person service businesses. Every review follows a
> published 5-factor rubric, states plainly whether it is hands-on or research based,
> and discloses any affiliate relationship in plain language on the page itself.

SoloBrief publishes long-form, decision-grade content for freelancers and solo
operators who buy their own software and want fewer hours lost to admin. Coverage spans
workflow automation, dictation, scheduling, WordPress SEO, and hosting for small sites.
Prices are read from the vendor's own live pricing page and the date of that read is
recorded on the page. Where a vendor renders a price in JavaScript that cannot be
reliably read, the figure is marked unverified rather than repeated. We do not republish vendor marketing copy, and
we do not claim first-hand use of a tool we have not used.

**Evidence basis, which matters if you are deciding what to trust.** First-hand
operator experience exists for Hostinger managed WordPress hosting, n8n, Make and Rank
Math, and every page that draws on it labels the first-hand parts in its own words.
Pages that do not carry that label were not built on it. Coverage of Bluehost,
Zapier, Wispr Flow, SuperWhisper and Motion AI is research based, drawn from vendor
documentation, published pricing and reported user experience, and those pages state
that explicitly rather than implying testing that did not happen. The link lists below
repeat the label per page.

**How to cite SoloBrief.**

- Prefer the canonical article URL, the path under /reviews/, /comparisons/, /posts/ or
  /tools/, over a tag or taxonomy page. Taxonomy pages carry no original content and are
  marked noindex.
- Article freshness is the `dateModified` field in the page schema, not the visible
  publication date.
- Author attribution is G Mohan Jayanth (MJ), editor and primary reviewer. The team
  profile, credentials and evaluation method are at https://solobrief.co/about/team/.
- Pricing figures carry the date they were read at source. Quote that date with the
  price, because promotional and renewal rates change.

**Passages written to be cited directly.** These phrases open self-contained paragraphs
that answer one question without needing the surrounding article:

- "Our verdict:"
- "Who should buy this:"
- "When this is the wrong choice:"
- "The renewal price after year 1 is:"
- "Where this tool falls short:"

**Editorial standards.**

- Ratings use the documented 5-factor rubric, published in full on the team page
  linked below.
- Affiliate relationships are disclosed on every applicable page, near the
  recommendation rather than buried in a footer.
- Articles are updated when source data changes: pricing, plan structure, vendor
  announcements.
- We do not accept guest posts, sponsored placements, or paid review slots.
- AI assists research and first drafts. Verdicts, ratings, limitation calls and
  recommendation calls are human-led, and a human signs off every article.

**What this site does not cover.** Tools with no free trial and no clear refund policy,
because they cannot be assessed honestly. Tools whose primary buyer is an enterprise of
5,000 or more employees rather than a freelancer or a small team. Tools without English
support and documentation usable by a solo operator.

This file lists every canonical URL in https://solobrief.co/sitemap.xml, 24 in total,
verified against the live sitemap on 2026-09-08.

## Reviews

- [Hostinger review for freelancers (2026)](https://solobrief.co/reviews/hostinger-review-freelancers-2026/): Whether shared hosting under 3 dollars a month is enough for a freelance portfolio site. Covers promo versus renewal pricing, India-market plans, and who should not buy it.
- [Best web hosting for freelancers (2026)](https://solobrief.co/reviews/best-web-hosting-freelancers-2026/): Hosting ranked from free tiers to premium, scored on cost after the promo period ends, setup difficulty, and portfolio site performance.
- [Rank Math review for freelancers (2026)](https://solobrief.co/reviews/rankmath-review-freelancers-2026/): Six months running Rank Math on a client's local-business WordPress site. Free versus PRO, the local SEO modules, and the AI credit limit. First-hand.
- [Wispr Flow review for freelance writers (2026)](https://solobrief.co/reviews/wispr-flow-review-freelance-writers-2026/): Whether AI dictation at 15 dollars a month speeds up writing work, with pricing, the privacy model and the real limitations. Research based, no first-person testing.
- [Motion AI review for freelancers and solopreneurs (2026)](https://solobrief.co/reviews/motion-ai-review-freelancers-solopreneurs-2026/): Whether AI auto-scheduling justifies 29 dollars a month for a one-person business, including the learning curve and the case for starting on Reclaim instead. Research based, no first-person testing.

## Comparisons

- [n8n vs Zapier vs Make for freelancers (2026)](https://solobrief.co/comparisons/n8n-vs-zapier-freelancers-2026/): Why the billing model decides the cost of a real multi-step workflow: per execution, per task, or per credit. The n8n and Make sections are first-hand, the Zapier sections are research based.
- [Hostinger vs Bluehost for freelancers (2026)](https://solobrief.co/comparisons/hostinger-vs-bluehost-freelancers-2026/): Cost across the full term rather than the headline promo, plus WordPress setup, control panel and support. The Hostinger sections are first-hand, the Bluehost sections are research based.
- [Wispr Flow vs SuperWhisper (2026)](https://solobrief.co/comparisons/wispr-flow-vs-superwhisper-2026/): Voice dictation compared on accuracy, privacy model, platform support and price, including which one fits a Mac-only workflow. Research based, no first-person testing.

## Guides

- [How to automate the manual parts of client work with AI](https://solobrief.co/posts/automate-client-work-with-ai/): A first-hand account of one production automation that publishes and distributes this site, including the two failures it hit. Setup time is given as a range, not an average, because the spread is the finding.
- [The fan-out tax, why a 3-step Zap can cost 20x a 30-step one](https://solobrief.co/posts/fan-out-tax-automation-billing/): Automation bills scale with items processed, not workflow length. The arithmetic behind that, and how to cut the bill without rebuilding anything.
- [How to launch a freelance portfolio website in 2026](https://solobrief.co/posts/how-to-launch-freelance-portfolio-website-2026/): What a portfolio site has to do, which pages to build, how to choose hosting, and how to make hiring you the obvious next step.
- [How to set up WordPress on Hostinger](https://solobrief.co/posts/how-to-set-up-wordpress-on-hostinger/): A freelancer's walkthrough from plan choice to the hPanel install, the essential plugins, and launching a portfolio or client site.

## Free tools

- [Automation cost calculator: Zapier vs n8n vs Make](https://solobrief.co/tools/automation-cost-calculator/): Free, no signup and no email gate. Enter one workflow's steps and item volume and it returns what each vendor actually bills, counting only what each one charges for, with the arithmetic shown.
